title: HTML Templates and Boilerplate
summary: A boilerplate is the standard starting skeleton — doctype, html/head/body, meta charset, viewport, title — that every page needs.

sections.content: A boilerplate is the standard starting skeleton — doctype, html/head/body, meta charset, viewport, title — that every page needs.
Templating (or components in frameworks) lets you reuse header/footer/nav across pages instead of duplicating markup.
Key points: always start from the boilerplate, charset UTF-8 first in head, viewport meta is required for mobile, and comments mark template regions.

sections.codeExample:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Page</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- content -->
</body>
</html>
